# Independent audit: allocated cap area measures and the planar section body

Source: `candidate 915dc3adcfe3fcf0`.

**Full Sections 1–5 PASS.** No repair requested. Independently reran the
expanded verifier: **2,529 exact checks PASS**.

## All allocations and cap laws

At a proper cut, the added section atom is at the outward normal of the
captured piece, namely (-u/|u|\). At an inside support, that is also the
old facet normal, so the body allocation and its complementary section
allocation sum to the full old facet mass. At an outside support the
two equal allocations lie at opposite normals. A homothetic subface of
the required intrinsic area realizes precisely those two atoms, including
zero mass. Lower-codimension touches contribute zero surface area.
These checks prove the recordwise identity for every status.

The effective representatives lie in the actual fiber. At an empty
record its arbitrary in-fiber point changes only translation and has
zero area measure. The selected points, homothetic face representatives,
and true cap intersections can be chosen measurably on the Borel status
strata. Their common compact bound makes their support functions
integrable for an arbitrary cap probability law. No finite cap selection
is used or needed.

The argument deliberately retains only normal area at an outside
support. A shorter face does not encode the original allocation's
tangential moments; the source expressly avoids that false inference.

## Orientation, balance and translated containment

Every effective area measure has zero vector moment, including the
two-atom lower-dimensional convention. Subtracting the aggregate old
surface measure therefore gives the oriented balance of (R\) with the
stated sign. Complementation reflects (R\) and keeps the same section
allocation.

In two dimensions, the distributional identity (S_K=h_K''+h_K\)
proves exact additivity for positive bodies, segments, points and their
bounded Minkowski integrals. The balanced nonnegative measure (R\)
therefore determines a convex (J\) up to translation. The described
rotated-normal curve construction has the correct orientation: relative
to its starting normal, its scalar projection decreases and then
increases back to the starting value, so that point is a support point.
Antipodal and zero measures give the stated degenerate bodies.

Since every effective representative lies inside its fiber, their
Minkowski integral (A\) lies inside the unweighted sum (B\). Equality
of area measures gives (A=\beta B+J+q\). Subtracting \(\beta h_B\)
from the support inequalities is legitimate and yields
\(J+q\subset(1-\beta)B\). The complementary integral independently
gives \(-J+q'\subset\beta B\); the two translations need not match.
The difference-body and area consequences follow as stated.

## Constants and actual midpoint geometry

For a centered triangle, the three normalized facet inequalities give
asymmetry exactly two. Under the explicitly stated homothetic-cap
hypothesis, (J=(a-a^2)T\) up to translation; the reflected containment
therefore gives (2(a-a^2)\le a^2\), exactly (a\ge2/3\). The actual
canonical centroid caps satisfy the required surface marginal: their
two edge portions have total length (4/3\) of that edge, and the
one-third cap weights give (4/9\). There is no assertion that arbitrary
caps reduce to this form.

The midpoint inclusion yields (K_-+K_0+K_+\subset3K_0\) with the
actual original translations. The crossed rectangles have endpoint
areas four, midpoint area \((R+R^{-1})^2\), and aggregate (3K_0\).
Thus \(|B|/M\to9\), proving exactly the claimed limitation of this
aggregate conversion. It does not prove sharpness of an actual critical
section-body ratio, and the source does not claim that.

## Affine base weighting and the precise loss

The weighted construction uses only nonnegative affine coefficients.
Normal-localized affine moment equality supplies its weighted section
balance; this is not guessed from the old unweighted circuit. Planar
degree-one surface addition then proves both weighted containments.
If the normalized weighted base mean is integer, actual compatibility
puts the weighted Minkowski sum in that one fiber. The resulting section
body is (J_\omega/\Omega\), not the original (J\).

On the complete three-point chain, affine weights have the form
\(A+Bz\); their mean is (2B/(3A)\), so integer mean zero forces
\(B=0\). In fact nonnegative weights allow no other integer mean.
Thus this case retains exactly the factor three.

The theorem supplies an oriented planar section body and translated
containments for the same actual cap law, including all supporting
allocations. It loses the base labels in the unweighted aggregate and
tangential allocation information in effective support faces. It gives
neither a parity-two reweighting nor a mixed Gamma payment.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
